messages:
Lina: quick re-run of the chat vs completions sizing experiment — did a focused pass on microbatch sizes + kernel selection after yesterday's p99 spike :point_up:
Mike: nice, which workload did you use? chat streaming sim or sync completions?
Lina: both. 50/50 mix to mirror prod, but separated runs for clean numbers. streaming chat used incremental token sends (stream enabled), completions were full-sync.
Anjali: what were baseline SLOs we cared about?
Lina: target p95 <= 200ms for inflection, p99 <= 600ms for chat streaming tail. for sync completions we allow higher p95 (~350ms) but want p99 < 900ms.
Rico: curious on kernel choices — did you force int8/quant kernels or let runtime choose?
Lina: forced three variants: fp16-default, int8-optimized, and `fallback-stable` that avoids attention-fusion on long seqs. let scheduler pick per-profile in one run, then pinned in another.
Mike: any KV-cache differences? streaming should reuse KV a lot which helps tail, right?
Lina: yes. streaming with client pinned session + persistent KV reduced compute by ~12% median. but we saw KV evictions when MBsize grew beyond 8 because per-batch memory ballooned and kernel started spilling.
Anjali: can you paste the profiling snippet?
Lina: sure:
```
== run: streaming_mb=2, kernel=auto ==
p50: 88ms, p95: 210ms, p99: 520ms
cpu/gpu util: 62/78
kv_hits: 94%, kv_evictions/min: 0.2
mb/second: 420
kernel_fallbacks: 0.1%
```
Lina: same run but mb=16:
```
p50: 130ms, p95: 340ms, p99: 820ms
cpu/gpu util: 85/96
kv_hits: 86%, kv_evictions/min: 2.3
mb/second: 980
kernel_fallbacks: 3.4%
```
Rico: wow p99 jump. fallbacks and evictions line up. kernel fallback probably due to OOM heuristics or tiling failures on int8 path.
Eva: did you capture kernel logs? that 3.4% fallback should show which op failed.
Lina: yes grabbed kernel debug trace — fallback mostly on `kv-merge` at long seqs (token > 1024) when batch has large variance. attached short excerpt: `kernel_run: int8_kv_merge -> OOM -> fallback(fp16)`
Mike: for sync completions, numbers?
Lina: sync completions (mb=8 auto-kernel):
```
p50: 155ms, p95: 360ms, p99: 740ms
kv_hits: 60%, kv_evictions/min: 1.7
mb/second: 520
kernel_fallbacks: 1.1%
```
Anjali: sync p95 close to our allowed 350-400, p99 is okay. interestingly kv_hits lower since completions don't reuse prefix as much.
Rico: so tradeoff summary: increasing MB reduces cost and increases throughput but hurts tail when KV evictions + kernel fallbacks occur. streaming is more sensitive at p99 because it expects low per-token tail for interactive SLO.
Lina: exactly. also observed hysteresis: after a fallback, next few requests on that worker had elevated latency due to kernel re-init. that's adding ~60-120ms on p99 samples.
Eva: what about splitting pools (small-batch low-latency vs big-batch high-throughput)? did you test routing?
Lina: yes — ran a split pool experiment with routing by estimated client latency budget (fast vs cheap). results:
- routing ~20% of traffic to small-batch pool (mb<=2) gives streaming p99 down ~35% with 8% cost increase overall.
- no split: p99 higher but cost 22% lower.
Mike: sounds like a clear product lever for tiered SLOs.
Anjali: any mitigation without pool split? like pre-warming kernels or forcing fp16?
Lina: pre-warm helps but is terraced: warms reduce first-request fallback but doesn't stop later evictions from memory pressure. forcing fp16 reduces fallbacks but increases tail in other cases because int8 path is faster when it works. it's a brittle win.
Rico: could we add a KV-eviction budget heuristic: if predicted batch will exceed memory threshold, either reduce MB at enqueue or prioritize sessions with warm KV?
Lina: I prototyped a simple reject/requeue when predicted KV > 75% mem. that cut p99 by ~18% on peak runs but dropped throughput during busy windows (fewer MBs formed).
Eva: tradeoff again. do we have regression evidence that kernel fallback rates increased after last runtime change?
Lina: yes — regression window aligns with the kernel-selector change on 2424800000. Fallbacks up from 0.6% -> 2.8% on mixed workloads.
Mike: rollback candidate or patch selector to prefer conservative fp16 when variance high?
Anjali: we should do targeted patch: selector heuristic that considers batch sequence-length variance and current KV footprint; prefer fp16 when variance > threshold or kv_free < X.
Rico: also better instrumentation: surface `kernel_fallback_reason` in per-request trace so SRE can alert on rising patterns.
Lina: agreed. Action items:
1) implement selector tweak (variance + kv_free) — Rico + Lina (ETA 2d)
2) add kernel_fallback_reason to traces & dashboard — Mike (ETA 3d)
3) run split-pool canary for 20% traffic to low-latency pool — Eva + Ops (ETA 5d)
4) collect longer-run cost delta and p99 impact (Anjali)

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: canary for split-pool will be staged at 2425080000 :robot_face:
Lina: thanks all. posting raw experiment logs to the perf-bench S3 bucket and will link in the dashboard.
Mike: thanks — moving to follow-up thread for selector PR once Rico/Lina start. :thumbsup:
